issue.title: Race between _PyObject_GenericGetAttrWithDict and ensure_nonmanaged_dict under free-threading

labels.name: type-bug
labels.description: An unexpected behavior, bug, or error

issue.body:
# Bug report

### Bug description:

Under Python 3.13.1t build with thread-sanitizer:
```python
import concurrent.futures
import functools
import threading

num_threads = 100


def closure(b, o):
  b.wait()
  getattr(o, "foo", None)
  o.foo = 42

with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=num_threads) as executor:
  for _ in range(100):
    b = threading.Barrier(num_threads)
    o = functools.partial(lambda x: x, 42)
    for _ in range(num_threads):
      executor.submit(functools.partial(closure, b, o))
```

comments.body:
I think there are two data races related to this:

1) The dictionary load in `_PyObject_GenericGetAttrWithDict` should be atomic (with *acquire* ordering since we're not using *consume*)
2) We need to handle the case where you change the dictionary (via `obj.__dict__ = newdict`). That doesn't show up in this example, but it's relevant since it may also race with the load. That was partly addressed in the following PR, but I don't think `PyObject_GenericSetDict` got updated. 

* https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/122489
I think it is worth adding ```_PyObject_GenericGetAttrWithDict```  here https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/117657 since it is reproducible in the manner described in this issue
Thanks @hawkinsp for the report and @wrongnull for the fix!
